mainTopic: Using the air between domains, and where an עירוב or שיתוף may be placed (gatehouses, sheds, courtyards), with רבי יהודה's rule on the owner's right of usage.
overview: The amud opens with the end of רב's ruling about two houses with three ruins between them. Each house may use the ruin next to it, but the middle ruin is forbidden to both. רב explains that the ruins stand in a triangle, so each side ruin can be reached by the far house only through the air, and the air does not forbid. The גמרא then defends שמואל, who holds that the air does forbid: that fence applies only to domains that are rabbinic. It also defends רב's ban on throwing between two houses across רשות הרבים: the concern is that the object may fall into the street, not the air. A new משנה teaches that an עירוב placed in a gatehouse, portico or balcony is invalid, and a resident there does not forbid. In storage sheds an עירוב is valid and a resident does forbid, unless, says רבי יהודה, the owner keeps a right of usage there. The גמרא works out where an עירוב and a שיתוף may be kept: an עירוב goes in a house, and a שיתוף goes in a courtyard. It applies this to a group whose meal ran into שבת. Finally, it gives the courtyard of בוניס as an example of a right of usage and begins a story about his son visiting רבי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The middle ruin is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The final clause of רב's ruling: of the three ruins between two houses, the middle one is forbidden to both houses.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the middle ruin is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the end of רב's ruling: each house may use the ruin next to it, but the middle ruin may not be used by either house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both houses have the same kind of access to the middle ruin, so neither one gets it, and each blocks the other. The side ruins are treated differently, and that difference is what the rest of this passage examines.

keyTerms.meaning: The middle one (here, the middle ruin)
Forbidden (to carry into or use on שבת)
A ruin, an abandoned plot between houses

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the subject of the whole conversation that follows. רבי אליעזר challenges it, and רב defends it.

phrases.english: And the middle one is forbidden.
phrases.notes: The end of רב's ruling about two houses with three ruins between them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב's ruling, which began in the text on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With three ruins between two houses, each house uses its adjacent ruin, and the middle ruin is forbidden to both.

steps.title: A student doubts the ruling is really from רב
steps.stepSummary: רב ברונא teaches the ruling in רב's name, and רבי אליעזר asks whether רב truly said it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ברונא was sitting and saying this teaching. רבי אליעזר, a student of the academy, said to him: Did רב really say this?
steps.whatsHappening: A story begins. רבי אליעזר hears רב ברונא quote the ruling and asks whether רב really said it. This sets up the challenge that comes later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He doubts the quote because he thinks the ruling clashes with something else רב said. That clash will be spelled out in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: Was sitting (often, teaching)
A teaching or ruling
A student of the academy
So, like this

phrases.english: Rav Beruna was sitting
and saying this teaching (in Rav's name).
phrases.notes: This refers to the ruling about the three ruins.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בַּר בֵּי רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer, a student of the academy, said to him:
phrases.notes: Some versions call him רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: Did Rav really say this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the ruling in step 1 is correctly attributed to רב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב actually made the ruling about the middle ruin.

steps.title: רב himself confirms the ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב ברונא says yes. רבי אליעזר goes to רב's lodging and asks him directly, and רב confirms it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. He said: Show me where he is staying. He showed him. He came before רב and said to him: Did the Master say this? He said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר does not rely on a quote. He goes to רב himself, and רב confirms he said the ruling. Now רבי אליעזר can bring his challenge directly to רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Getting רב's own confirmation removes any chance that the ruling was misquoted. So the challenge that follows must be answered on its logic, not by saying 'רב never said it.'

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
Show me
Lodging, place where one stays
The Master (a respectful way to address a teacher)

phrases.english: He (Rav Beruna) said to him: Yes.
(He said:) Show me his lodging.
He showed him.
He came before Rav,
and said to him: Did the Master say this?
He said to him: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2, first through רב ברונא and then through רב himself.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. רב himself confirms that he made the ruling.

steps.title: Challenge from רב's ruling on lowering and throwing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר points out that רב himself ruled: when one side reaches a place by שלשול and the other by זריקה, both are forbidden. Easier access does not win.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But isn't it the Master who said: For this one by lowering and for that one by throwing, both are forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר now challenges רב with a contradiction from רב's own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Assume the ruins stand in a straight line. Then the far house could also reach the near ruin, just less easily, through the air. If each house still wins its adjacent ruin, that must be because its access is easier. But רב ruled elsewhere that easier access (שלשול versus זריקה) does not give one side the place: both are forbidden. So why should the side ruins be permitted?

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it the Master who said (introduces a contradiction from the speaker's own words)
Lowering something down
Throwing something
Both are forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר is not saying the middle ruin should be permitted. His problem is with the side ruins: why are they permitted to the nearby house when the other house also has some access to them?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, וְהָא מָר הוּא דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: He said to him: But isn't it the Master who said:
(a place usable) for this one by lowering
and for that one by throwing —
both are forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רב has confirmed the ruling, רבי אליעזר shows how it seems to contradict another ruling of רב's.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's permission for each house to use its adjacent side ruin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ruins are in a line, both houses can reach each side ruin, one more easily than the other. But רב holds that easier access does not give one side the place (שלשול versus זריקה, both forbidden). So the side ruins should be forbidden too.

steps.title: The ruins stand in a triangle, not a line
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the three ruins are arranged כחצובה, in a triangle, not כשורה, in a line.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do you think they stand in a row? No, they stand like a tripod.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the challenge by correcting the picture of the case: the ruins form a triangle, not a straight line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a triangle, the middle ruin touches both houses directly and equally, so it is forbidden to both. Each side ruin touches only its own house directly. The other house could reach it only through the air of its own ruin, and that kind of access does not forbid. So the reason the side ruins are permitted is not easier access, and there is no contradiction with the שלשול and זריקה ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you think? (introduces a correction of a mistaken assumption)
In a straight row
Like a tripod, in a triangle
Air (access through the air does not forbid)

steps.whatToRemember: רב: with two houses and three ruins arranged in a triangle, the middle ruin, touching both houses equally, is forbidden. Each side ruin belongs to its adjacent house, because the other house reaches it only through the air, and that does not forbid. This fits רב's other ruling that easier access alone (שלשול versus זריקה) does not give one side a place.

phrases.english: He said to him: Do you think
that they stand in a row?
No — they stand like a tripod (in a triangle).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4 by changing the layout of the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruins stand in a straight line, so each side ruin is permitted only because of easier access, which contradicts רב's ruling on שלשול and זריקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruins form a triangle. Each side ruin is directly reachable only by its own house, while the other house reaches it only through the air, which does not forbid. The middle ruin is equally reachable by both, so it is forbidden.

steps.title: Does שמואל disagree with רב דימי's report?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא suggests that שמואל's view, that the air between domains can forbid, contradicts רבי יוחנן's ruling (reported by רב דימי) that a small spot between רשות הרבים and רשות היחיד may be used by both sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: Shall we say that שמואל does not agree with רב דימי? When רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A place that is less than four by four טפחים may be used by both the people of רשות הרבים and the people of רשות היחיד to rest their loads on, as long as they do not swap objects through it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא raises a problem for שמואל. רבי יוחנן lets two different domains share a small spot, and that seems to ignore any worry about the 'air' between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says one side can forbid a place to the other through the air. רבי יוחנן says that when a small spot sits between two domains, both sides may use it. The only limit is that they may not pass things to each other through it. So it looks like רבי יוחנן does not care about the air, and the question is whether שמואל argues with that.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? Introduces a suggested conclusion, often one the גמרא will reject
He does not hold of (this view)

keyTerms.term: מָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אַרְבַּע עַל אַרְבַּע
keyTerms.meaning: A spot smaller than 4x4 טפחים, which counts as a מקום פטור (exempt area)
To adjust or rest a load on one's shoulder
Swap or exchange objects (between the two domains)

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not challenging רב here. The target is שמואל, who is the one who says the air can forbid.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא שְׁמוּאֵל לֵית לֵיהּ דְּרַב דִּימִי.
phrases.english: Shall we say that Shmuel does not hold of Rav Dimi's teaching?
phrases.notes: שמואל holds that a place can be made forbidden even through the air.

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: For when Rav Dimi came (from Eretz Yisrael), he said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אַרְבַּע עַל אַרְבַּע —
phrases.english: A place that is not four by four handbreadths
phrases.notes: This kind of spot is called a מקום פטור, an exempt area.

phrases.english: is permitted for the people of the public domain
and for the people of the private domain to adjust their loads on it,
as long as they do not exchange objects (through it).

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא שְׁמוּאֵל לֵית לֵיהּ דְּרַב דִּימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line testing שמואל's 'air forbids' view against רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that one can forbid a place to another through the air
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן lets two domains share a small in-between spot without any air concern. That seems to contradict שמואל.

steps.title: Torah domains versus rabbinic domains
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that רבי יוחנן's case involves domains of Torah law, while our case involves domains of rabbinic law, and the חכמים reinforced their own rules more.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the domains are from the Torah. Here, the domains are rabbinic. And the חכמים made extra safeguards for their own words, more than for the Torah's.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends שמואל by showing that the two cases are different kinds of domains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רשות הרבים and רשות היחיד are Torah categories. People take Torah law seriously, so no extra fence about the air was needed. Carrying between private areas without an עירוב is only forbidden מדרבנן. Because people might treat rabbinic rules lightly, the חכמים added a stricter fence, which is the air rule. So שמואל does not argue with רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in the other case)
Here (in our case)
From Torah law
From rabbinic law
Reinforcement or safeguard

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known principle that appears in several places: the חכמים sometimes made their own rules stricter than Torah rules, so that people would not take them lightly.

phrases.english: There, the domains are of Torah law,
here, the domains are of rabbinic law.
And the Sages made reinforcement for their words
more than for those of the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם — רְשׁוּיוֹת דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, הָכָא — רְשׁוּיוֹת דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (Torah domains vs. rabbinic domains)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל seemed to argue with רבי יוחנן about the air.
steps.terutzMaskana: No argument. The air rule is an extra rabbinic fence that applies only to rabbinic domains.

steps.title: רב forbids throwing between two houses
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks whether רב really holds that the air does not forbid, since רב forbids throwing from one house to another across a public street.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רבא: Did רב really say this? But it was taught: Two houses on two sides of רשות הרבים. רבה בר רב הונא said in רב's name: It is forbidden to throw from one to the other. And שמואל said: It is permitted to throw from one to the other!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges רב's position from another ruling of רב himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב was understood to hold that one does not forbid a place to another through the air. Yet here רב forbids throwing between two houses that face each other across a public street. That looks like a worry about the air of רשות הרבים in between, which would contradict רב's own view.

keyTerms.meaning: Did רב really say this?
But it was stated (an אמוראים dispute)
To throw
From one to the other

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is aimed only at רב. שמואל's permission to throw is not a problem: it fits step 7, since the street between the houses is a Torah domain, where שמואל's rabbinic air rule does not apply.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rava:
Did Rav really say this?
phrases.notes: Did רב really say that the air doesn't make a place forbidden?

phrases.english: But wasn't it stated:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי בָתִּים מִשְּׁנֵי צִידֵּי רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
phrases.english: Two houses on two sides of a public domain,

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
It is forbidden to throw from one to the other,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: מוּתָּר לִזְרוֹק מִזֶּה לָזֶה!
phrases.english: and Shmuel said: It is permitted to throw from one to the other!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמַר רַב הָכִי? וְהָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from שמואל to test רב's own consistency.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that one does not forbid a place to another through the air
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב forbids throwing over the public street between two houses, which seems to be a worry about the air in between.

steps.title: One house is higher than the other
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that רב's ruling was set in a case where one house is high and the other low. A thrown object might roll back into the street, and someone might carry it in.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Didn't we already explain that one house is high and the other low? Sometimes the object rolls and falls, and the person will come to bring it in.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends רב by explaining that his ruling against throwing has a different reason, not the air.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The houses are at different heights. When you throw upward, the object might not land and could fall into רשות הרבים. The thrower might then go and carry it from the street into his house, which is a Torah-level violation. So רב's ban is a practical safeguard, and it does not contradict his view that the air does not forbid.

keyTerms.meaning: We established (the case as)
One is high and one is low
Rolls
To bring it (carry it in)

steps.whatToRemember: Both apparent contradictions are resolved. שמואל's air rule is a special rabbinic fence for rabbinic domains. רב's ban on throwing is about the object falling into the street, not about the air.

phrases.english: He (Rava) said to him:
Didn't we establish (the case)
that one house is high and one is low,
sometimes it rolls and falls (into the public domain),
and he will come to bring it in.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו מִי אוֹקֵימְנָא דְּמִדְּלֵי חַד וּמִתַּתֵּי חַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא), giving a different reason for the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב forbade throwing because of the air of רשות הרבים.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב forbade throwing only because the object might fall into the street and be carried in.

steps.title: Gatehouse, portico and balcony: not a valid place for an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that an עירוב placed in a gatehouse, portico or balcony is not valid, and someone living there does not forbid carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone puts his עירוב in a gatehouse, a portico, or a balcony, it is not a valid עירוב. And a person who lives there does not forbid carrying for the homeowner.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It names three open, entrance-type areas of a חצר and gives two rules about them: an עירוב placed there does not work, and a person living there does not forbid carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These spaces are passageways or open structures, not real homes. So they are not a proper 'house' in which to keep the עירוב. For the same reason, someone staying there is not counted as a resident whose missing share would forbid carrying for everyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (the opening text that the גמרא will discuss)
Food collected from all residents and kept in one house, which lets them carry within the shared courtyard on שבת
Gatehouse: a small entrance structure at the gate of a courtyard
Portico: a roofed area with no walls, or with incomplete walls
Balcony
Forbids: a resident who did not join the עירוב makes carrying forbidden for everyone

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate rules here. One is about where you may PUT the עירוב. The other is about whether a PERSON LIVING there forbids carrying. Do not mix them up.

phrases.english: MISHNAH
One who places his eiruv in a gatehouse,
a portico, or a balcony —
it is not a valid eiruv.
And one who lives there —
does not forbid carrying for him (the homeowner).
phrases.notes: Even if he did not contribute to the עירוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַנּוֹתֵן אֶת עֵירוּבוֹ בְּבֵית שַׁעַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. It is unrelated to the preceding discussion of air between domains.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gatehouse, portico and balcony: an עירוב there is invalid, and a resident there does not forbid carrying.

steps.title: Storage sheds: a valid place for an עירוב, and a resident there forbids
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that an עירוב placed in a hay shed, cowshed, woodshed or storehouse is valid, and someone living there does forbid carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: A hay shed, a cowshed, a woodshed, or a storehouse: an עירוב placed there is valid. And a person who lives there forbids carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the opposite list. These are storage buildings where an עירוב works, and where a person living there does forbid carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the open entrance areas in the previous step, these are closed, guarded buildings that count as real rooms. So the עירוב can be kept there. A person living there counts as a true resident, and if he did not join the עירוב, he forbids carrying for the rest of the חצר.

keyTerms.meaning: Hay shed
Cowshed
Woodshed
Storehouse

phrases.english: A hay shed or a cowshed
or a woodshed or a storehouse —
this is a valid eiruv,
and one who lives there forbids carrying.
phrases.notes: This applies if he did not contribute to the עירוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting case to step 10: real enclosed structures instead of open entrance areas.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Storage sheds: an עירוב there is valid, and a resident there forbids carrying.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: if the homeowner keeps usage rights, the resident does not forbid
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that if the homeowner keeps a right to use the shed, the person living there does not forbid carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: If the homeowner keeps a right of use there, the person living there does not forbid carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a limit to the previous rule. If the homeowner still uses part of that shed, the person staying there does not forbid carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the homeowner keeps a 'hold' on the space, the room still counts as part of the homeowner's own property. The person living there is then treated like a member of the homeowner's household, not a separate resident. So his missing share in the עירוב does not forbid anyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'a hold of the hand': a right to use the space, fully or partly
The homeowner

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If there is there a right of usage
belonging to the homeowner —
he (the resident) does not forbid carrying.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two kinds of places. In open entrance areas, an עירוב does not work and a resident does not forbid. In real storage rooms, an עירוב works and a resident does forbid, unless (according to רבי יהודה) the homeowner still uses the room.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם יֵשׁ שָׁם תְּפִיסַת יָד שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the rule in step 11 that a resident of a storage shed forbids carrying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the homeowner keeps usage rights in the shed, the person living there does not forbid carrying.

steps.title: רב יהודה's two general rules, each with an exception
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בריה דרב שמואל בר שילת teaches two rules. First: wherever a resident does not forbid, an עירוב placed there is invalid, except an individual's gatehouse. Second: wherever an עירוב cannot be placed, a שיתוף can be, except in the airspace of the מבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יהודה, son of רב שמואל בר שילת, said: Any place where the חכמים said that a person living there does not forbid carrying, an עירוב placed there is not valid, except a gatehouse belonging to one individual. And any place where the חכמים said an עירוב may not be placed, a שיתוף may be placed, except the open airspace of the מבוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with an אמורא who turns the משנה into two general rules, each with one exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rule one links the two halves of the משנה: a place too weak to make its resident count also cannot hold an עירוב. The exception is a gatehouse used by only one person, where the עירוב is valid. Rule two says that a שיתוף, which joins courtyards into an alley, only needs to be somewhere inside a courtyard. So it may sit in a gatehouse or portico, but not out in the open alley itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
A gatehouse belonging to, and used by, only one individual
Merging of alleyways: joining the courtyards that open onto a shared alley (מבוי) so that carrying is allowed in the alley
The open airspace of the alley itself, which is not inside any courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: עירוב and שיתוף are different tools. An עירוב joins houses in one courtyard and must be kept in a house. A שיתוף joins courtyards into an alley and only needs to be kept inside a courtyard.

phrases.english: GEMARA

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat, said:
Any place about which they said
that one who lives there does not forbid carrying —
one who places his eiruv there, it is not a valid eiruv,
except for a gatehouse of an individual.
phrases.notes: There, the resident does not forbid, yet an עירוב placed there is valid.

phrases.english: And any place about which the Sages said
that one may not place an eiruv there —
one may place a merging of alleyways there,
except for the airspace of the alleyway.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Generalizes the משנה's lists (steps 10 and 11) into two broad rules with exceptions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 1) Where a resident does not forbid, an עירוב placed there is invalid, except an individual's gatehouse. 2) Where an עירוב may not be placed, a שיתוף may be, except the airspace of the מבוי.

steps.title: What does רב יהודה add? The משנה already teaches it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב יהודה's statement teaches. The משנה already says an עירוב in a gatehouse, portico or balcony is invalid, and its wording implies that a שיתוף works there.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned in the משנה: if someone puts his עירוב in a gatehouse, portico or balcony, it is not a valid עירוב. That means it is not valid as an עירוב, but it is valid as a שיתוף!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's second rule as seemingly unnecessary. It is setting up a question that will be answered in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says only that an עירוב does not work in these places. Reading closely, that wording implies a שיתוף would work there. So the rule 'where an עירוב can't go, a שיתוף can' seems to be already in the משנה, and the גמרא wants to know what new point רב יהודה is adding.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is he teaching us?' A challenge saying a statement seems to add nothing new
'We already learned it' (in a משנה or ברייתא)
'But then...' The word that introduces an inference drawn from what a text says

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned:
One who places his eiruv in a gatehouse
a portico, or a balcony —
it is not a valid eiruv.
It is an eiruv that it is not,
but a merging of alleyways it is?
phrases.notes: If we read the משנה's wording this way, the second rule would seem unnecessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second rule of step 13 as already implied by the משנה in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's two rules as a whole. The first is stated outright in the משנה, and the second (where an עירוב may not be placed, a שיתוף may be) is implied by the משנה's wording.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording 'it is not an עירוב' already implies that a שיתוף works there, so the rule seems to add nothing new.

steps.title: The rule was needed for the two cases the משנה did not teach
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה's rules were needed for the two exceptions, an individual's בית שער and the airspace of a מבוי, because the משנה never mentions them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rules were needed for an individual's gatehouse and for the airspace of an alleyway, because the משנה does not teach these cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 14. רב יהודה was not repeating the משנה. He was adding two cases the משנה never mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only gives the general pattern of where an עירוב does or does not work. רב יהודה adds two new exceptions: a gatehouse that belongs to one person, and the open airspace of the מבוי. Those two exceptions are the new information.

keyTerms.meaning: A gatehouse that belongs to one person
The open airspace of the alleyway
It was necessary for him (to say)
Which we did not learn (in the משנה)

phrases.english: A gatehouse of an individual
and the airspace of an alleyway
were necessary for him to teach, since we did not learn them (in the משנה).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the new information: the exceptions the משנה left out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה's rule just repeats the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: His rule adds two exceptions the משנה never taught

steps.title: A ברייתא that seems to support this
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that an עירוב placed in a gatehouse, portico, balcony, courtyard or alleyway is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: One who puts his עירוב in a gatehouse, portico, balcony, courtyard or alleyway, this is an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as support. Its wording is about to cause a problem, so this step sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists places that, according to the משנה, are not homes, and still says the food placed there works. Read plainly, it clashes with the משנה. The גמרא will correct its wording, and then it will match רב יהודה's idea that a שיתוף can go where an עירוב cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a supporting ברייתא)
Portico, a roofed area open on the sides
Balcony

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
One who places his eiruv in a gatehouse,
a portico, or a balcony,
or in a courtyard, or in an alleyway —
this is an eiruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רב יהודה's rule
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's rule that a שיתוף can be placed where an עירוב cannot
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing places where the food is valid

steps.title: But the משנה says this is not an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא contradicts the משנה, which says an עירוב in a gatehouse, portico or balcony is not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: this is not an עירוב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא says the opposite of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (step 10) said that an עירוב placed in a gatehouse, portico or balcony is not valid. The ברייתא calls the same thing a valid עירוב, so the two sources clash.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in a משנה)?

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: this is not an eiruv!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא from step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's words "הרי זה עירוב" (this is an עירוב)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא cannot contradict an explicit משנה

steps.title: Read it as a valid שיתוף
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is corrected to say the food is a valid שיתוף, not an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: this is a שיתוף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the ברייתא's wording so it no longer clashes with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These places are not homes, so the food cannot work as an עירוב for a courtyard. It can still work as a שיתוף for the alleyway. This matches רב יהודה's rule that a שיתוף works where an עירוב does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read the text this way instead)
Shared food that joins the courtyards of an alleyway

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up עירוב and שיתוף. An עירוב joins the houses of one courtyard and must be placed in a house. A שיתוף joins courtyards into the alleyway and can be placed in places like these.

phrases.english: Say instead: this is a merging of the alleyway (shituf).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by correcting the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא calls it a valid עירוב
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means a valid שיתוף

steps.title: A שיתוף in the open alleyway is not guarded
steps.stepSummary: Even as a שיתוף, food left in the open alleyway is not guarded, so it should not be valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a שיתוף placed in the alleyway is not guarded!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the corrected version, because the ברייתא still lists the alleyway itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food left in the open alleyway can easily get lost or taken, so it does not count. This also fits רב יהודה's exception that a שיתוף cannot be placed in the airspace of the מבוי.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not guarded

phrases.english: But a shituf in the alleyway is not guarded?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the corrected reading from step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The word "ובמבוי" in the corrected ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unguarded food cannot serve as a שיתוף

steps.title: Read it as a courtyard within the alleyway
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is corrected again: it means a courtyard that opens onto the alleyway, not the open alleyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: in a courtyard that is in the alleyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a second fix so the ברייתא fully fits the rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A courtyard is enclosed, so food there is guarded and can serve as a שיתוף. The open airspace of the alleyway stays excluded, exactly as רב יהודה said.

keyTerms.meaning: A courtyard that opens onto the alleyway

steps.whatToRemember: The corrected ברייתא says a שיתוף works in a gatehouse, portico, balcony, or a courtyard on the alleyway, but not in the open alleyway. This matches רב יהודה's rule.

phrases.english: Say instead: in a courtyard that is in the alleyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 by correcting the ברייתא again
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שיתוף is in the open alleyway
steps.terutzMaskana: The שיתוף is in a guarded courtyard on the alleyway

steps.title: A dining group may rely on the bread on the table as an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: שמואל teaches that if שבת starts while a group is eating together, the bread on their table counts as an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: A group that was dining together when שבת began may rely on the bread on the table as an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. שמואל gives a ruling about a group whose meal ran into שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once שבת starts, they can no longer set up an עירוב. Still, the bread they all share on the table already joins them, so it counts as an עירוב for carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: A group of people eating together
Reclining, that is, dining together
The day became holy for them; שבת began
They may rely on it

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
A group of people who were dining together
and the day became sanctified for them (Shabbat began),
the bread that is on the table —
they may rely on it as an eiruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about relying on shared bread
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bread on a dining group's table counts as an עירוב

steps.title: Another version: the bread counts as a שיתוף
steps.stepSummary: Another version of שמואל's statement says the bread counts as a שיתוף instead of an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: as a שיתוף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of what שמואל said. This sets up רבה's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree that the bread helps. They seem to argue about what it helps for: joining a courtyard (עירוב) or joining the alleyway (שיתוף).

keyTerms.meaning: And some say it (another version)

phrases.english: And some say: as a shituf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative version of step 21
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bread counts as a שיתוף

steps.title: רבה: the two versions do not argue
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that both versions are right. In a house the bread is an עירוב, and in a courtyard it is a שיתוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: They do not argue. Here they are dining in the house, and there they are dining in the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה shows that the two versions of שמואל are talking about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב must be placed in a house. So if the group eats indoors, the bread works as an עירוב for the courtyard. If they eat in the courtyard, it cannot be an עירוב, but it can be a שיתוף for the alleyway, since a שיתוף may sit in a courtyard (as seen in step 20).

keyTerms.meaning: And they do not argue
Here — there (two different cases)

steps.whatToRemember: Eating indoors makes the bread an עירוב. Eating in the courtyard makes it a שיתוף. The same rule runs through the whole section: an עירוב needs a house, while a שיתוף can be in a courtyard.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the new topic back to the earlier rules about where an עירוב and a שיתוף may be placed.

phrases.english: Rabba said: And they do not disagree:
here — where they are dining in the house,
there — where they are dining in the courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the apparent dispute between steps 21 and 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the case by location (house vs. courtyard)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two versions disagree about what the bread counts as
steps.terutzMaskana: In a house the bread is an עירוב, and in a courtyard it is a שיתוף

steps.title: אביי brings a source that supports רבה
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רבה that a ברייתא supports him: עירובי חצרות are placed in a courtyard, and שיתופי מבואות are placed in an alleyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבה: There is a ברייתא that supports you. עירובי חצרות are placed in the courtyard, and שיתופי מבואות are placed in the alleyway.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a ברייתא as proof for רבה's explanation that both versions of שמואל are correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said the bread is an עירוב in a house and a שיתוף in a courtyard. The ברייתא gives each type of joining its own location, which is the same kind of split. The exact wording still has to be fixed, and the next steps do that.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
That supports you
Joinings of courtyards (houses joined into one courtyard)
Mergings of alleyways (courtyards joined into one alleyway)

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rabba:
A baraita was taught that supports you:
Joinings of courtyards are placed in the courtyard,
and mergings of alleyways are placed in the alleyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבה's resolution from step 23
steps.raayaObject: רבה's rule: an עירוב belongs in a house and a שיתוף belongs in a courtyard
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that gives separate locations to עירובי חצרות and שיתופי מבואות

steps.title: The ברייתא clashes with the משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי continues and recalls a question that was once raised on this ברייתא: how can an עירוב be placed in a courtyard, when a משנה says an עירוב placed in a gatehouse, portico, or balcony is not valid?
steps.simpleTranslation: We once discussed this ברייתא and asked: Can עירובי חצרות really be placed in a courtyard? Didn't we learn in a משנה that if someone places his עירוב in a gatehouse, a portico, or a balcony, it is not an עירוב?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי, still speaking, recalls an earlier challenge to the wording of the ברייתא he just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says an עירוב does not work in open or in-between areas such as a gatehouse, a portico, or a balcony. A courtyard is also not a real place to live. So an עירוב placed in the open courtyard should be invalid as well.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (an earlier challenge we raised)
Gatehouse
Portico (a roofed area that is open on its sides)
Balcony

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a brand-new attack on רבה. אביי is retelling an earlier discussion about the wording of this ברייתא, so that the corrected reading is clear.

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
Joinings of courtyards are placed in the courtyard?
But didn't we learn in a mishna:
One who places his eiruv
in a gatehouse, a portico, or a balcony
it is not an eiruv!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא brought in step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that עירובי חצרות are placed in the courtyard
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules that an עירוב in a non-dwelling area is invalid, and the open courtyard is such an area.

steps.title: The ברייתא is reread: house in the courtyard, courtyard in the alleyway
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא really means that an עירוב goes in a house within the courtyard, and a שיתוף goes in a courtyard within the alleyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it this way: עירובי חצרות are placed in a house that is inside the courtyard, and שיתופי מבואות are placed in a courtyard that is inside the alleyway.
steps.whatsHappening: Still within אביי's report, the ברייתא's wording is corrected so it no longer clashes with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each joining is placed one level down, inside the area it serves. An עירוב sits in a house within the courtyard, and a שיתוף sits in a courtyard that opens onto the alleyway. This corrected reading is exactly רבה's split: a house for the עירוב and a courtyard for the שיתוף.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read the text this way instead)
In a house that is in the courtyard
In a courtyard that is in the alleyway

steps.whatToRemember: An עירוב of courtyards is placed in a house. A שיתוף of an alleyway is placed in a courtyard. This is why רבה said the bread at a meal is an עירוב in a house and a שיתוף in a courtyard.
steps.whyThisMatters: The corrected ברייתא gives a clear practical rule for where each kind of joining must be kept, and it confirms רבה's resolution of the two versions of שמואל.

phrases.english: Say instead:
Joinings of courtyards are placed in a house that is in the courtyard;
mergings of alleyways are placed in a courtyard that is in the alleyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25 and so completes the proof for רבה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to allow an עירוב in the open courtyard itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עירוב goes in a house within the courtyard, and the שיתוף goes in a courtyard within the alleyway. This supports רבה.

steps.title: What counts as a right of usage?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה in the משנה, who says the resident does not forbid if the owner has תפיסת יד there, and asks what that case looks like.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יהודה says, if the owner has a right of usage there, and so on. What is the case of a right of usage?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and asks for a concrete example of רבי יהודה's term תפיסת יד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that someone living in a storage shed, such as a hay shed or cowshed, does forbid carrying for the courtyard. רבי יהודה adds an exception: the resident does not forbid if the owner keeps a right of usage in that space. The גמרא wants to know what this right of usage actually looks like.

keyTerms.meaning: Right of usage (the owner keeps his things or his access in the space)
What is the case? What does it look like?
Etc. (the rest of the quoted text)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ שָׁם תְּפִיסַת יָד וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: If there is a right of usage there, etc.
What are the circumstances of a right of usage?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the גמרא returns to explain the next clause of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete example of תפיסת יד

steps.title: An example: the courtyard of בוניס
steps.stepSummary: An example of תפיסת יד is the courtyard of בוניס, a rich man who kept his belongings in the rooms where others lived.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, the courtyard of בוניס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a famous real-life case, the courtyard of בוניס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בוניס was so wealthy that he stored his things in the rooms of the people living on his property. Because he could come in and use those rooms, they still counted as his. The people living there were treated like members of his household, so they do not forbid the courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: For example
בוניס, a very wealthy man

phrases.english: For example, the courtyard of Bonyas.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The courtyard of בוניס, where the owner's belongings filled his residents' rooms

steps.title: רבי honors the son of בוניס
steps.stepSummary: A story: בן בוניס came before רבי, and רבי told his attendants to make room for someone worth one hundred מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן בוניס came before רבי. רבי said to his attendants: Make room for a man worth one hundred מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The mention of בוניס leads the גמרא into a story about his son visiting רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story moves away from the laws of עירוב and shows how rich the בוניס family was. רבי gave בן בוניס honor that matched his wealth. The story continues with a second visitor.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא
Make room
A unit of money (one hundred זוז)

phrases.english: The son of Bonyas came before Rabbi;
he said to them (his attendants):
Make room for one who owns one hundred maneh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story linked by association to בוניס from step 28
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי showed honor to the wealthy בן בוניס

steps.title: Another visitor arrives
steps.stepSummary: Another person came before רבי, and רבי began to speak to his attendants. His words continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another person came, and רבי said to them:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line that brings in a second visitor. It prepares for what רבי will say next, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story is building a contrast between the first visitor and this one. רבי's actual statement about the second man is not on this amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Another person

phrases.english: Another person came;
he said to them:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of step 29 and sets up the next statement
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only. רבי's statement follows on the next amud.
